II. Statement of Substance of Interview
Applicant thanks the Examiner for the courtesies extended during the interview

conducted November 22, 2022. During the interview, Applicant's representative and the Examiner discussed the Office Action and the reasoning for the rejections in view of Beijing Qihoo Tech. No agreements were reached.
It is respectfully submitted that the instant STATEMENT OF SUBSTANCE OF
III. Claim Rejections - 35 U.S.C. § 102
Claims 1-20 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as allegedly being anticipated by CN109151068 to Beijing Qihoo Tech.

Applicant respectfully submits that the Office Action failed to establish how "each and every one" of the claimed features is believed to be disclosed by Beijing Qihoo Tech. In the Office Action, the recitations of the claims appear to be "cut and pasted" onto pages 2-5 of the Office Action with reference to pages of Beijing Qihoo Tech at the end of each line of the claim. However, no reasoning is provided explaining why the citations from Beijing Qihoo Tech are believed to disclose the claimed features in each line, nor are the citations matched to the features of the claims. Applicant respectfully submits that the rejection is improper at least in view of the following.

MPEP @ 2131 states that "' [a] claim is anticipated only if each and every element as set forth in the claim is found, either expressly or inherently [See related post] described, in a single prior art reference.' Verdegaal Bros. v. Union Oil Co. of California, 814 F.2d 628, 631, 2 USPQ2d 1051, 1053 (Fed. Cir. 1987)" (emphasis added). "'The identical invention must be shown in as complete detail as is contained in the ... claim.' Richardson v. Suzuki Motor Co., 868 F.2d 1226, 1236, 9 USPQ2d 1913, 1920 (Fed. Cir. 1989)" (emphasis added). Moreover, "[e]very element of the claimed invention must be literally present, arranged as in the claim." Id. (emphasis added). In the present case, the Office Action has not established that each element of the claims is disclosed in Beijing Qihoo Tech. The Office Action merely appended page numbers to the end of each paragraph of the claims with no reasoning or association with the claimed features.

Furthermore, Beijing Qihoo Tech fails to meet the strict identity requirement to prove anticipation. A rejection under @ 102 requires a showing of strict identity between the rejected claim and a disclosure in the cited reference. Trintec Indus., Inc. v. Top-U.S.A. Corp., 295 F.3d 1292, 1296 (Fed. Cir. 2002). To meet the strict identity requirement, all elements must be disclosed, in a single reference, in exactly the same way as they are arranged or combined in the claim. Therasense, Inc. v. Beton, Dickinson & Co., 593 F.3d 1325, 1332 (Fed. Cir. 2010). "
For example, Independent claim 1 recites:
A cloud application-based resource transfer method, performed by a terminal,
the method comprising:
displaying, through a cloud application, a video interface generated after
processing through a cloud;
displaying, in response to a trigger operation on a target visual element in
the video interface used for triggering resource transfer, a resource transfer
channel interface generated by the cloud;
displaying a target resource transfer channel in the resource transfer
channel interface;
displaying resource transfer-related information corresponding to the
target resource transfer channel and generated by the cloud; and
triggering, in response to a resource transfer confirmation operation for the
resource transfer-related information, a resource transfer operation that is based on the resource transfer-related information through the target resource transfer
channel.
Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 is patentable, and claim 1 is not anticipated, because Beijing Qihoo Tech fails to disclose all of the claim's features, including those reproduced above.

For example, in rejecting the features of claim 1, the Examiner cites Beijing Qihoo Tech at pages 9, 11, and 21 as allegedly teaching "A cloud application-based resource transfer method, performed by a terminal, the method comprising: displaying, through a cloud application, a video interface generated after processing through a cloud." See Office Action at p. 2. Applicant respectfully submits that Beijing Qihoo Tech, at best, discloses "operating data of the specific application, such as display data and sound data is through a cloud service to transmit to the mobile terminal, such as a personal computer device, to provide to the user." See Beijing Qihoo Tech at page 2, 3. However, Beijing Qihoo Tech is silent as to "[Dlisplaying, through a cloud application, a video interface generated after processing through a cloud."
The Examiner also cites Beijing Qihoo Tech at pages 11-12, 15-17, and 19-22 as

allegedly teaching "displaying, in response to a trigger operation on a target visual element in the video interface used for triggering resource transfer, a resource transfer channel interface generated by the cloud; displaying a target resource transfer channel in the resource transfer channel interface;." See Office Action at pp. 2-3. Applicant respectfully submits that Beijing Qihoo Tech, at best, discloses "after the task name and task content to generate to-be- processed data to be processed by the task, the client function data task is sent to the cloud service to be processed by the cloud service data task set/identifier request allocation of cloud

data." See Beijing Qihoo Tech at page 11, 1. However, Beijing Qihoo Tech is silent as to "displaying, in response to a trigger operation on a target visual element in the video interface used for triggering resource transfer, a resource transfer channel interface generated by the cloud; displaying a target resource transfer channel in the resource transfer channel inter face."
The Examiner also cites Beijing Qihoo Tech at pages 11-12, 15-17, and 19-22 as

allegedly teaching "displaying resource transfer-related information corresponding to the target resource transfer channel and generated by the cloud." See Office Action at p. 3. Applicant respectfully submits that Beijing Qihoo Tech, at best, discloses "the source cloud application 402 to the application server 420 includes changing the content of status change request, wherein the state change request may include updated content 402 associated with the source cloud application and associated with the updated content of the update condition." See Beijing Qihoo Tech at page 16, 5. However, Beijing Qihoo Tech is silent as to "displaying resource transfer- related information corresponding to the target resource transfer channel and generated by the cloud."
The Examiner also cites Beijing Qihoo Tech at pages 11-12, 15-17, and 19-22 as

allegedly teaching "triggering, in response to a resource transfer confirmation operation for the resource transfer-related information, a resource transfer operation that is based on the resource transfer-related information through the target resource transfer channel." See Office Action at p.

3. Applicant respectfully submits that Beijing Qihoo Tech, at best, discloses "cloud source application 402 based on changing content to generate task name and task content,." See Beijing Qihoo Tech at page 17, 1. However, Beijing Qihoo Tech is silent as to "triggering, in response to a resource transfer confirmation operation for the resource transfer-related
information, a resource transfer operation that is based on the resource transfer-related information through the target resource transfer channel."

For at least the above reasons, Applicant respectfully submits claim 1 is patentable over the cited art and is not anticipated. Independent claims 9 and 17 are patentable over the cited art for at least similar reasons as claim 1 due to their similarly recited subject matter. Applicant further respectfully submits dependent claims 2-8, 10-16, and 18-20 are patentable over the cited art for at least the same reasons as independent claims 1, 9, and 17 by virtue of their dependencies therefrom.
Additionally, Applicant respectfully submits that the dependent claims also cite features not disclosed in Beijing Qihoo Tech. For example, claim 4 recites:
The cloud application-based resource transfer method according to claim

1, wherein the triggering, in response to a resource transfer confirmation operation for the resource transfer-related information, a resource transfer operation that is based on the resource transfer-related information through the target resource
transfer channel comprises:
determining a resource transfer application corresponding to the target
resource transfer channel in response to the resource transfer confirmation
operation for the resource transfer-related information; and
jumping from the cloud application to the resource transfer application,
and transferring the resource transfer-related information into the resource transfer application, to cause the resource transfer application to perform the resource
transfer operation based on the resource transfer-related information.
Applicant respectfully submits that claim 4 is patentable, and claim 4 is not anticipated, because Beijing Qihoo Tech fails to disclose all of the claim's features, including those reproduced above.
The Examiner cites Beijing Qihoo Tech at pages 11-12, 15-17, and 19-22 as allegedly
teaching all of the features of claim 4 See Office Action at p. 3. However, Applicant respectfully submits Beijing Qihoo Tech is completely silent as to "jumping from the cloud application to

the resource transfer application, and transferring the resource transfer-related information into the resource transfer application, to cause the resource transfer application to perform the resource transfer operation based on the resource transfer-related information."
For at least the above reasons, claim 4 is also patentable over the cited art.
IV. Conclusion
